subject: Re: Urgent: LumenHealth latency spike — evidence suggests client-side timeouts
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@lumenhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@lumenhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-29T08:13:00-05:00
Subject: Latency spikes — hitting p95/p99, urgent

Rachel —

We started seeing a sharp regression yesterday evening. p95 is up ~2.5x and p99 is spiking above our SLA (tail hits 6–8s intermittently) for the text-generation endpoint. Our app experienced user-visible errors and many client-side timeouts. We opened this with our SRE team; they captured a bunch of client logs and a few request IDs (attached).

Can you confirm whether this is a backend regression or something on our side? This is affecting a production rollout tomorrow; we need clarity quickly.

Attached: sdk-logs-20261128.txt (client logs), sample-request-ids.txt

—Alex
Director, Platform Engineering
LumenHealth
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@lumenhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T08:45:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Latency spikes — hitting p95/p99, urgent

Alex — thanks for the quick heads up and for the logs. We're treating this as high priority. Initial checks: no deploy around the time window on the Redwood side, and infra metrics show elevated tail latency correlated with increased request concurrency for that account. We'll run a focused correlation between your request IDs and our traces in the next hour.

I’m looping in engineering (Sergio + Markus) to verify whether we're seeing service-side anomalies vs. client retry amplification. I will update you with a timeline and immediate mitigation options (fallback rules, rate-limiting) within 90 minutes.

—Rachel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T08:52:00-05:00
Subject: Fwd: Latency spikes — LumenHealth (urgent)

Team — forwarding LumenHealth escalation. Key points:
- Customer reports p95/p99 regressions starting 11/28 evening (US).
- They observed client-side timeouts and attached SDK logs.
- No Redwood deploy at the time.

Ask: can infra/runtime take a quick look for (a) request amplification (retries in short windows), (b) KV cache miss patterns, (c) GPU queueing/backpressure for that tenant pool? If we can identify whether retries are originating client-side vs server-side, it changes the ask to the customer.

I can provide the sample request IDs and the Datadog link. If this looks like a customer-side retry loop, we should prepare a short explanation for their SREs and an ops playbook to reduce the observed tail.

—Rachel
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:25:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Latency spikes — LumenHealth (urgent)

I've started pulling traces and the per-tenant queue metrics. Quick summary:
- We see bursts of near-simultaneous requests from LumenHealth at 21:14–21:16 UTC on 11/28. Token-serialized latencies look normal for single requests, but there's a pattern where identical request IDs appear with different timestamps — suggests retries.
- GPU-side utilization climbed but did not saturate; however, concurrency caused queueing delays at the worker pool level.
- No internal autoscaler flapping or recent kernel changes.

My hypothesis: client-side timeout (short deadline) + immediate retry in SDK leads to amplification under transient congestion, inflating p95/p99. I’ll correlate the SDK logs they sent against our request IDs and share a mapping.

—Sergio
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T10:12:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Latency spikes — LumenHealth (urgent)

Following Sergio's work, I pulled a trace subset and matched client log entries. Findings:
- Several request_ids from the customer's logs correspond to three attempts within ~2s windows. The SDK default timeout was set to 1.2s in their config; when the server tail ran to ~1.6–2.2s those calls hit client deadlines and retried immediately.
- Retries are not being de-duplicated by the client (no idempotency key) and our load balancer treats them as new requests. That multiplies work and worsens the tail.
- We do see a small number of server-side 503s during the peak window (backpressure / queue saturation), but they appear downstream of the retry storm rather than the root cause.

Recommendation:
1) Short-term mitigation: enable per-tenant early-bail (a conservative concurrency cap + queue-length backpressure) for LumenHealth today to stop amplification. It is a config toggle in the routing layer.
2) Customer-facing: communicate that our signals show client-side timeouts+retries amplified congestion; ask them to increase SDK deadline to 5s or enable exponential backoff + idempotency token as a best practice.
3) Medium-term: add server-side detection (simple dedupe by client-request-id header within 3s window) and a telemetry doc for partners.

I'll prepare the configuration patch and a short ops runbook.

—Markus
Lead, Inference Runtime
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T11:02:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Latency spikes — hitting p95/p99, urgent

Alex — update from eng after correlating your logs to our traces: short summary for your SREs and execs below.

What we saw:
- Customer logs show repeated attempts (3x) for the same request IDs within ~2s when server tail latency crossed ~1.5s.
- Those retries were accepted as separate requests by our routing layer and amplified worker queueing, increasing p95/p99 for the tenant.
- We observed a handful of 503s that appear to be downstream consequences of the amplification, not the initiating event.

Immediate actions we are taking (next 60–120m):
- Flip a conservative per-tenant concurrency cap and queue backpressure for LumenHealth to reduce amplification impact. (This is a routing config toggle; low-risk.)
- Roll a hotfix to log client-request-id headers to make short-term dedupe easier for investigatory work.

Customer asks for you:
- Increase SDK deadline from 1.2s to 5s for production traffic or enable exponential backoff between retries.
- If possible, add an idempotency/request-id header on generation calls so that retries can be deduped.

Executive note: if you would like us to proceed with the per-tenant cap immediately, say the word and we’ll enact it and monitor. We’ll also draft a brief postmortem and a partner-facing best-practices note.

Attachments: lumen_prod_traces.zip (sample server traces correlated to your request IDs)

—Rachel
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@lumenhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@lumenhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-30T11:02:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Latency spikes — hitting p95/p99, urgent

Rachel — thanks for the clear analysis and quick mitigation. Please go ahead and enable the per-tenant cap; we’ll push SDK changes (deadline/backoff + idempotency header) in the next deploy window.

We may need a short executive note for our CTO; could you and Markus put together a 1-page summary of root cause and actions by EOD?

—Alex
